rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3.2 and 4 (Figures 8-14) - the author builds a fuzzy controller in LabView Fuzzy System Designer for greenhouse temperature/air speed and humidity/irrigation time and reports the simulation outputs as his own result.
rows.notes: The study is a pure LabView simulation of a fuzzy on-off controller (temperature setpoint 15 C; irrigation time as a function of humidity). It reports no measurement of water or energy use, and the simulation output is never compared with observations from a real greenhouse (the methodology mentions 'verified during the real-time implementation' but no data, plant or validation are presented; the greenhouse model figure is taken from ref [43]). The study therefore shows only that the controller logic can be programmed and responds to deviations from the setpoint in simulation, which is at most a precondition of the claimed optimisation of water and energy use, not evidence of it. No triangulation, no intermediate variable measured, single simulated site, no field or farm scale, no stated conditions or limitations beyond generic future-work statements, no dispersion measures.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through bibliography). Figures are not reproduced but their captions indicate only simulation screenshots. Note the claim also frames the technology as app_scheduling; the study is a fuzzy logic controller simulation in LabView, which loosely matches the passage's 'fuzzy logic controllers', so technology mismatch was not flagged.
